title: Knowledge check: Cache-Control and Security Headers

questions.prompt: How should an API communicate the outcome of an operation?
options: Return a stack trace to help clients infer the failure category.
Use a status code with the correct HTTP meaning and include stable headers and a safe response representation where appropriate.
Return 200 for all outcomes and put the real status only in a private server log.
Use 401 whenever a record is missing, regardless of authentication state.
questions.answer_key: Use a status code with the correct HTTP meaning and include stable headers and a safe response representation where appropriate.
questions.explanation: Use a status code with the correct HTTP meaning and include stable headers and a safe response representation where appropriate. This is especially relevant to “Cache-Control and Security Headers” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Cache-Control and Security Headers”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Assert the status code, required headers, response shape, and safe error behavior.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
questions.answer_key: Assert the status code, required headers, response shape, and safe error behavior.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Cache-Control and Security Headers”?
options: The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
Status codes contradict the outcome or errors reveal internal details.
questions.answer_key: Status codes contradict the outcome or errors reveal internal details.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
